native_warning.evidence: Both R68 archives give the same Key_Carrier notice as every slice since R58, including the approved R63, R66 and R67 pairs. The evidence comes from each archive's own layers.json and verify.log. In both, completely_unsupported_starts is [] for all 13 parts and native_support_moves is 0; the primary carrier covers 312 layers and 1,898,461 samples. Both verify.log files show blocked [] and unsupported_starts {}, and the geometry jobs exited 0. Each archive has only four one-anchored runs, all outside the restore box (Y 20.9-43.66). Two are at layer 11 (1.015 and 2.158 mm), at the inherited rear-socket stations beside the rod. Two are at layer 155 (3.666 and 6.346 mm), at Y ~12.65, Z ~10.5; both pairs match R66/R67. The R66/R67 layer-49 outboard-lip start is gone, because the restored lip now rises from the bed, yet the notice persists. So that line was never its trigger, and the earlier association should be retired. The layer-10 and layer-195 runs also disappeared, at unchanged geometry. Inside the restore box the only reviewed runs are two two-anchored ~1 mm runs at layer 59 (X ~-21.5, Z 4.1 and 6.25, Y ~31.85). They are the unchanged spring-shoe ends, as in R66, and nothing sits at lip height. The 1.41 mm two-anchored lead-in bridge at layer 164 is retained. The slicer does not say where its notice comes from. It is accepted as the known notice, not as a reason for supports.

Report labelling. In op1-route.json, the top-level three_holes and seat_support_mm2 blocks carry only r63/r66 keys, because relabel renames only r67. There, 'r66' holds the current carrier's values, so the README's statement that r66 is the R66 reference is wrong for those blocks. The lead_in block's r66/r68 keys are correct and are the ones cited above.

Service access is not checked by geometry. R68 has pack sweeps only: there is no battery lead or connector route check, and no hand-access check. With the full outer wall restored, removal relies on gripping the 5.25 mm exposed pack end, as in R64.
residual_unknowns: Freeing the base at R64's corner ties. This placement has never been printed, and R63's lip-rooted fins needed heavy twisting. The -y fin also sits partly under the lip's wall-side root.
Battery insertion, spring preload, retention and removal with the real pack, and how its lead exits the open end.
The white plug is a photo-estimated envelope: threading from below and orientation are unproven. The lead-in guides only at the deck's own underside edge, and approach_below_deck is descriptive only.
Whether the keeper holds the board down, and whether clicks repeat.
Collet grip on the real tube.
PETG stringing or sag at the 1.41 mm layer-164 lead-in bridge, the layer-155 one-anchored runs and the inherited long bridges.
The source of the floating-regions notice, which the slicer does not identify.
physical_checks: Watch the first ~3 mm of the carrier (corner ties, restored wall foot and lip start on the bed) and layer 155.
Cut both corner ties flush before peeling, without twisting against the spring-root post. Inspect the wall foot, the lip root and the free leaf.

Compare the real white plug with the 3.1 x 6.2 x 3.65 mm envelope. Thread it from below with the rod and guards installed, mate it above, seat the board on the three sockets, then fit the switch, paddle and keeper and check repeated clicks.
Test pouch insertion, retention, removal and lead exit, and collet grip. Use the standard pin and the clip; keep the spare.
